description: (0.5.0) A change entry is a hint until verified (RFC-ACDP-0018 §7), plus the consumer's cursor, resync, idempotency, revocation-matching and discovery duties. Behavioral, consumer-side.

expected.behavior: The golden lifecycle entry verifies (event signature, event receipt per RFC-ACDP-0017 §10.3, full-list retraction state) and the consumer marks its reliance for re-evaluation.
Same entry with one byte of event.signature.value flipped: no reliance decision changes; the consumer re-verifies the context directly.
event_receipt.index does not match the event's position: treated as absent; no reliance change.
Entry is index 1 and the consumer has not verified index 0: it MUST re-retrieve the full list before applying.
superseded_by's retrieved body does not supersede ctx_id (or has a different lineage_id): no reliance change.
A key_revocation entry whose verified revocation is out of producer scope (RFC-ACDP-0014 §7): no reliance change.

The same verified entry delivered twice leaves the same reliance state as delivering it once (idempotent processing). Deduplicating by (authority, seq) is allowed only between resyncs (RFC-ACDP-0018 §7 Idempotency).
On cursor_expired the consumer re-verifies every watched context directly, then resumes from since=head.

scenarios.name: I — invalid_cursor on a persisted cursor

expected.behavior: The consumer polls with a next_cursor it persisted from an earlier response and the registry answers invalid_cursor (400). The consumer treats it exactly as cursor_expired: it re-verifies every watched context directly, clears its (authority, seq) dedup state for that authority, and resumes from since=head. It MUST NOT stop watching or retry the same cursor forever.

scenarios.name: J — seq reused after a resync

expected.behavior: Before a resync the consumer processed seq 1042. After the resync (scenario H or I), the feed serves a different entry at seq 1042. The consumer verifies and processes it as a new entry; it MUST NOT drop it as a duplicate.

scenarios.name: K — revocation matched by the retrieved fingerprint

expected.behavior: A key_revocation entry names controller D. The consumer relies on two contexts by D, signed by different keys. It retrieves and verifies the revocation and matches metadata.revoked_key_fingerprint from that signed body: only the context signed by the revoked key is marked for re-evaluation (subject to RFC-ACDP-0014 §7's compromise boundary); the context signed by D's other key is unchanged. The entry itself carries no fingerprint, and the consumer MUST NOT match on anything but the retrieved, verified value.

scenarios.name: L — feed silence is not non-revocation

expected.behavior: The producer of a relied context publishes a key revocation to a different registry. The feed of the serving registry carries no key_revocation entry. The consumer still learns of the revocation through its scheduled RFC-ACDP-0014 §8 discovery for that producer; it MUST NOT treat the absence of a feed entry as evidence the key is unrevoked.

scenarios.name: M — a short page is not the head

expected.behavior: The consumer sends limit=500 to a registry whose max_changes_page is 100. The registry returns 100 entries with has_more: true. The consumer requests again at once from next_cursor; it MUST NOT conclude from the clamped or filtered page size that it reached the head. Only has_more: false says no committed entry lies past next_cursor.
